name: addpipe16_ripple4_prefix12_fixedcin
rationale: Prior ripple+prefix hybrid attempt (ripple3_sklansky13) underperformed the frontier's own ripple2_prefix14/ripple6_prefix10 points because it injected the ripple carry-in via an extra post-tree OR-merge stage (adding one full logic level of delay) instead of folding it into the base-level generate signal at the very first prefix stage, which is how true carry-in injection should work (no extra depth). This candidate fixes that structural bug: a short 4-bit ripple computes c3 (carry out of bit 3), which is folded directly into the local generate signal gl'[0] = g[4] | (p[4] & c3) feeding a standard 4-stage Sklansky prefix tree over the remaining 12 bits -- exactly matching the depth budget of the already-strong ripple2_prefix14/ripple6_prefix10 frontier members but at an untried split (4-ripple/12-prefix) that should land in the currently-unfilled area gap between ripple6_prefix10 (293.4 area/7.32 wns) and ripple2_prefix14 (334.6 area/7.56 wns), plausibly producing a new non-dominated area/WNS point (potentially beating addpipe16_sklansky's 319.2 area/7.49 wns since it has one fewer 'wasted' logic level than my earlier buggy hybrid attempt).
